'''Richard Vershaun Seymour''' (born October 6, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Richard Seymour Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SeymRi00.htm |access-date=2024-05-04 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[New England Patriots]] and [[Oakland Raiders]].  He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]], and was drafted by the Patriots sixth overall in the [[2001 NFL draft]].

Seymour played in seven [[Pro Bowl]]s, was named to five [[All-Pro]] teams, and was a member of three [[Super Bowl]]-winning Patriots teams. During his career, Seymour was considered to be one of the best defensive linemen in the NFL.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/football/nfl/patriots/2006-05-31-seymour-sw_x.htm|title=If you have just one lineman, make it Seymour|work=[[USA Today]]|first=Chris|last=Colston|date=May 31, 2006|access-date=May 18, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/news?slug=jc-offday101106&prov=yhoo&type=lgns|title=Breakfast of champions|work=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|first=Jason|last=Cole|date=October 11, 2006|access-date=May 18, 2009}}</ref> Seymour was elected into the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 2022.

Seymour was selected to the [[Pro Bowl]] both as a 3-4 defensive end and as a 4-3 defensive tackle. He occasionally played [[Fullback (American football)|fullback]] on short yardage and goal line situations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.ign.com/articles/565/565952p2.html|title=Richard Seymour Interview|work=[[IGN]]|first=Jon|last=Robinson|date=November 12, 2004|access-date=May 18, 2009}}</ref> However, it was stopped when he suffered a knee injury on a one-yard [[Corey Dillon]] touchdown run against the [[San Diego Chargers]] in October 2005.<ref name="Fullback">{{Cite web |date=October 8, 2005 |title=Patriots will be without DE Seymour against Atlanta |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2185140 |access-date=May 19, 2009 |website=[[ESPN.com]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> After his football career, he became a professional [[poker]] player.

'''Richard Marlon Wood''' (born May 31, 1953) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] played who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[New York Jets]] and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans]], earning [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors. '''Richard Arlen Osborne''' (October 31, 1953 – February 26, 2025) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] for four seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Osborne played his high school football at [[Robert E. Lee High School (San Antonio, Texas)|Robert E. Lee High School]] in San Antonio where he earned all-state honors as a wide receiver. He helped lead the Lee Volunteers to a 28-27 1971 UIL 4A State title over Wichita Falls high school.   [[Tommy Kramer]] who had a long NFL career was his quarterback in high school. Another notable teammate in high school was [[Pat Rockett]] who also earned all-state honors and later played Major League Baseball for the Atlanta Braves.

Osborne died on February 26, 2025, at the age of 71.<ref>[https://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/article/richard-osborne-lee-high-school-football-20196225.php Richard Osborne, a San Antonio football legend, has died at 71]</ref>
